posts.title: Rod Shoate: Unanimous All-American Linebacker in 1974
posts.question: Which Oklahoma linebacker was a unanimous All-American on the 1974 national champions?
posts.answer: Rod Shoate, a linebacker from Spiro, Oklahoma, was a consensus All-American in 1973 and a unanimous selection in 1974, when Oklahoma went 11-0 and won the national championship. He entered the College Football Hall of Fame in 2013.
posts.summary: Rod Shoate (OU 1972-74) was a consensus All-American in 1973, unanimous in 1974, and a 2013 College Football Hall of Fame inductee. Read his Sooner story.

posts.title: Oklahoma 44, Baylor 34: First Visitor to Win at McLane
posts.question: When did Oklahoma beat Baylor 44-34 at McLane Stadium in 2015?
posts.answer: On November 14, 2015, No. 12 Oklahoma beat No. 6 Baylor 44-34 in Waco. The Sooners ended Baylor's 20-game home winning streak and became the first visiting team to win at McLane Stadium.
posts.summary: On Nov. 14, 2015, No. 12 Oklahoma won 44-34 at No. 6 Baylor, ending a 20-game home streak and becoming the first visitor to win at McLane Stadium.

posts.title: Jerry Tubbs: Unanimous 1956 All-American Center at OU
posts.question: Which Oklahoma center was a unanimous All-American in 1956 and finished fourth for the Heisman?
posts.answer: Jerry Tubbs, who played for Oklahoma from 1954 to 1956, was a unanimous All-America center in 1956 and finished fourth in that year's Heisman Trophy voting. He was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 1996.
posts.summary: Jerry Tubbs moved from fullback to center under Bud Wilkinson, played on 31 straight OU wins, and became a unanimous 1956 All-American and Hall of Famer.

posts.title: Eddie Crowder: OU Quarterback Who Led Colorado Football
posts.question: Which former Oklahoma quarterback became Colorado's head football coach and athletic director?
posts.answer: Eddie Crowder, an All-American quarterback for Bud Wilkinson's Sooners in 1952, became Colorado's head coach in 1963 and also served as the school's athletic director from 1965 to 1984.
posts.summary: Eddie Crowder quarterbacked Bud Wilkinson's Sooners to an All-America 1952 season, then coached Colorado to a 67-49-2 record and ran its athletic department.

posts.title: Oklahoma and Texas Tech Set the FBS Yardage Record in 2016
posts.question: What is the FBS record for combined yards in a game, and did Oklahoma play in it?
posts.answer: Oklahoma's 66-59 win at Texas Tech on October 22, 2016, produced 1,708 combined yards, an FBS record at the time. Each team finished with 854 yards, topping the 1,640 San Jose State and Nevada totaled in 2001.
posts.summary: Oklahoma beat Texas Tech 66-59 in 2016 in a game that produced an FBS-record 1,708 combined yards, with 854 for each team. Here is how it happened.

posts.title: Josh Heupel Finishes Second for the 2000 Heisman Trophy
posts.question: Who was Oklahoma's quarterback runner-up for the 2000 Heisman Trophy?
posts.answer: Josh Heupel finished second to Florida State's Chris Weinke in the 2000 Heisman voting, 1,628 points to 1,552. He was also named the AP College Football Player of the Year before leading Oklahoma to a 13-0 national championship season.
posts.summary: Josh Heupel was the 2000 Heisman runner-up, just 76 points behind Chris Weinke, and led Oklahoma to a 13-0 national title. Here is how it unfolded.

posts.title: Tommy McDonald Wins the 1956 Maxwell Award at Oklahoma
posts.question: Which Oklahoma halfback won the 1956 Maxwell Award?
posts.answer: Halfback Tommy McDonald won the 1956 Maxwell Award as the nation's top college player and finished third in that year's Heisman Trophy voting. He later reached both the College Football Hall of Fame and the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
posts.summary: Tommy McDonald won the 1956 Maxwell Award, placed third for the Heisman, and went on to two Halls of Fame. Here is the story of the Sooner halfback.

posts.title: Jason White's 18 Straight Completions vs. Nebraska, 2004
posts.question: How many passes in a row did Jason White complete against Nebraska in 2004?
posts.answer: Jason White completed 18 consecutive passes, a school record, in Oklahoma's 30-3 win over Nebraska on November 13, 2004. He finished 29 of 35 for 383 yards and three touchdowns.
posts.summary: On Nov. 13, 2004, Jason White hit a school-record 18 straight passes and threw for 383 yards as No. 2 Oklahoma beat Nebraska 30-3 in Norman.

posts.title: Did Oklahoma Have the "Play Like a Champion Today" Sign First?
posts.question: Did Oklahoma use the Play Like a Champion Today sign before Notre Dame?
posts.answer: Yes, by the available evidence. OU says Bud Wilkinson hung a "Play Like a Champion Today" sign over the Sooners' locker room door in 1947 or 1948, decades before Lou Holtz put up Notre Dame's famous version for the 1986 season.
posts.summary: OU says Bud Wilkinson hung a Play Like a Champion Today sign in 1947 or 1948, long before Notre Dame's 1986 version. Here is the evidence fans should know.

posts.title: The Sooner Schooner Penalty: What Happened at the 1985 Orange Bowl
posts.question: Did the Sooner Schooner really cause a penalty in the 1985 Orange Bowl?
posts.answer: Yes. In the January 1, 1985 Orange Bowl against Washington, the Schooner rolled out to celebrate a field goal that had been wiped out by a penalty, drawing a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct flag. The longer kick was blocked and OU lost 28-17.
posts.summary: In the Jan. 1, 1985 Orange Bowl, the Sooner Schooner celebrated a nullified field goal, drew a 15-yard flag, and OU lost 28-17 to Washington. The full story.

posts.title: Why Are OU's Colors Crimson and Cream? The 1895 Origin Story
posts.question: When did the University of Oklahoma choose crimson and cream as its colors?
posts.answer: OU's colors were chosen in the fall of 1895 by a committee chaired by student May Overstreet, which picked crimson and cream. The colors have shifted toward crimson and white over time, but fans still call them crimson and cream.
posts.summary: OU picked crimson and cream in fall 1895, when a committee led by May Overstreet chose the colors. Here is why fans still say cream though the look is white.

posts.title: When Did OU's Boomer and Sooner Mascots Debut? The 2005 Big Red Rally
posts.question: When were the Boomer and Sooner costumed mascots introduced at Oklahoma?
posts.answer: OU's costumed mascots Boomer and Sooner were introduced at the Big Red Rally on campus on August 26, 2005, after nearly three years of development. They are named for the real ponies that pull the Sooner Schooner.
posts.summary: Boomer and Sooner, OU's costumed mascots, debuted at the Big Red Rally on Aug. 26, 2005. Learn how they connect to the real Sooner Schooner ponies.

posts.title: Who Are the RUF/NEKS? OU's Spirit Squad and Its 1915 Roots
posts.question: Who are the RUF/NEKS at Oklahoma and how did they get their name?
posts.answer: The RUF/NEKS are OU's all-male spirit squad, founded in 1915 and billed as the oldest male spirit group in college sports. The name comes from "roughnecks," an insult a fan hurled at the noisy students that they adopted with pride.
posts.summary: The RUF/NEKS, OU's all-male spirit squad, date to 1915 and took their name from a fan who called them roughnecks. They drive the Sooner Schooner today.

posts.title: Oklahoma's Bowl Streak: How Many Straight Years in the Postseason?
posts.question: How many consecutive bowl games has Oklahoma played in?
posts.answer: Oklahoma played in a bowl game 26 straight seasons, from 1999 through the 2024 Armed Forces Bowl, then reached the College Football Playoff in 2025. That makes 27 consecutive postseason appearances through the 2025 season.
posts.summary: OU went bowling 26 straight seasons from 1999 through the 2024 Armed Forces Bowl, then made the 2025 CFP, a 27-year postseason run. Here is how it stacks up.

posts.title: "The Day the Pride Won": OU's Band and the 1983 Bedlam Comeback
posts.question: What was The Day the Pride Won in Oklahoma football history?
posts.answer: "The Day the Pride Won" was Oklahoma's 21-20 comeback at Oklahoma State on October 15, 1983, when the Pride of Oklahoma band kept playing "Boomer Sooner" as OU rallied from 20-3 down. Barry Switzer gave the band an honorary game ball.
posts.summary: On Oct. 15, 1983, OU rallied from 20-3 to win at Oklahoma State 21-20 while the band played Boomer Sooner nonstop. Switzer gave the band an honorary game ball.

posts.title: How Many Consensus All-Americans Has Oklahoma Produced?
posts.question: How many consensus All-Americans has Oklahoma football had?
posts.answer: Through the 2025 season, Oklahoma has produced 83 consensus All-Americans, sixth-most among FBS programs, out of 169 first-team All-Americans overall. Linebacker Danny Stutsman (2024) is the most recent.
posts.summary: Oklahoma has 83 consensus All-Americans, sixth in FBS, plus 169 first-team picks and 35 unanimous. See the firsts, two-time honorees and latest Sooner.

posts.title: Pride of Oklahoma History: OU's Band Since 1904 and Its Sudler Trophy
posts.question: When was the Pride of Oklahoma marching band founded and has it won the Sudler Trophy?
posts.answer: The Pride of Oklahoma traces to 1904, when freshman Lloyd Curtis founded OU's first continuous student band. The band received the Sudler Trophy, one of college marching band's most prestigious national honors, in 1987.
posts.summary: The Pride of Oklahoma dates to 1904, when Lloyd Curtis started OU's first continuous student band. It won the Sudler Trophy in 1987. Here is its history.

posts.title: Most Heisman Winners by School: Where Does Oklahoma Rank?
posts.question: Which school has the most Heisman Trophy winners, and how many does Oklahoma have?
posts.answer: Oklahoma has seven Heisman Trophy winners, tied with Notre Dame and Ohio State for second-most behind USC's eight through the 2025 award. OU is also the first school with Heisman-winning quarterbacks in back-to-back seasons.
posts.summary: Oklahoma has seven Heisman winners, tied with Notre Dame and Ohio State behind USC's eight. Here is the full list and the back-to-back QB first OU owns.

posts.title: Who Wrote the OU Chant? Jessie Lone Clarkson Gilkey's 1936 Alma Mater
posts.question: Who wrote the OU Chant and when was it written?
posts.answer: The OU Chant, Oklahoma's alma mater, was written in 1936 by Jessie Lone Clarkson Gilkey, who directed the university's girls' glee club from 1936 to 1938. Fans traditionally raise one index finger while it plays.
posts.summary: The OU Chant was written in 1936 by glee club director Jessie Lone Clarkson Gilkey. Learn the history of OU's alma mater and the raised-finger tradition.

posts.title: How Many All-Time Wins Does Oklahoma Football Have?
posts.question: How many all-time wins does Oklahoma football have, and where does it rank?
posts.answer: Through the 2025 season, Oklahoma's all-time record was 960-351-53, a winning percentage of about .723. The Sooners rank sixth in major college football history in both total wins and winning percentage.
posts.summary: Oklahoma football went 960-351-53 through 2025, sixth in college football history in wins and win rate. See which coaches won the most games.

posts.title: Who Wrote Boomer Sooner? The 1905 Origin of OU's Fight Song
posts.question: Who wrote the Boomer Sooner fight song and where does the tune come from?
posts.answer: OU student Arthur M. Alden wrote the words to "Boomer Sooner" in 1905, setting them to the tune of Yale's "Boola Boola." A year later a section borrowed from North Carolina's "I'm a Tar Heel Born" was added.
posts.summary: Boomer Sooner began in 1905 when OU student Arthur M. Alden put words to Yale's Boola Boola tune. A Tar Heel addition came in 1906. Here's the full story.

posts.title: How Many Conference Titles Has Oklahoma Won? 50, Most in FBS
posts.question: How many conference championships has Oklahoma football won?
posts.answer: Oklahoma has won 50 football conference championships, shared titles included, the most of any FBS program through the 2025 season. The total includes 33 in the Big Six/Seven/Eight lineage and 14 in the Big 12.
posts.summary: Oklahoma owns 50 football conference titles, the most in FBS, including 14 Big 12 crowns and a 14-year Big Eight streak. Here is the full breakdown.

posts.title: What Does "Sooner" Mean? The 1889 Land Run and OU's Nickname
posts.question: What does Sooner mean and why are the Oklahoma football teams called the Sooners?
posts.answer: A "Sooner" was a settler who slipped into Oklahoma's Unassigned Lands before the legal start of the April 22, 1889 Land Run. OU's teams took the Sooners nickname in 1908 after about a decade as the Rough Riders or Boomers.
posts.summary: A Sooner jumped the gun in the April 22, 1889 Land Run. Learn how the term became OU's team nickname in 1908 after years as the Rough Riders and Boomers.

posts.title: What Is the Longest Play in Oklahoma Football History?
posts.question: What is the longest play in Oklahoma Sooners football history?
posts.answer: The longest play from scrimmage in Oklahoma history is Abdul Adams's 99-yard touchdown run at Baylor on Sept. 23, 2017. On returns, several Sooners have gone the full 100 yards, most recently Billy Bowman Jr. with a 100-yard interception return at BYU in 2023.
posts.summary: Abdul Adams's 99-yard TD run at Baylor in 2017 is OU's longest play from scrimmage. Here are the longest passes, punt returns and 100-yard returns too.

posts.title: When Did the Sooner Schooner Debut? The 1964 Story Behind OU's Wagon
posts.question: When did the Sooner Schooner first appear at an Oklahoma football game?
posts.answer: The Sooner Schooner made its first appearance at Owen Field on September 26, 1964, when USC beat Oklahoma 40-14. The covered wagon and its ponies became an official OU mascot in 1980.
posts.summary: The Sooner Schooner debuted at Owen Field on Sept. 26, 1964, versus USC and became OU's official mascot in 1980. Here is how the wagon tradition began.

posts.title: Most Passing Yards in an OU Game: Baker Mayfield's 598 at OSU
posts.question: What is the most passing yards in a single game by an Oklahoma quarterback?
posts.answer: Baker Mayfield threw for 598 yards in Oklahoma's 62-52 win at Oklahoma State on Nov. 4, 2017, the Sooners' single-game passing record through the 2025 season. Landry Jones is second with 554 yards at West Virginia in 2012.
posts.summary: Baker Mayfield passed for 598 yards in a 62-52 Bedlam win at Oklahoma State in 2017, the OU single-game record. See the rest of the top passing games.

posts.title: 2019 Peach Bowl: LSU 63, Oklahoma 28 and Burrow's Record Half
posts.question: What happened when Oklahoma played LSU in the 2019 Peach Bowl?
posts.answer: No. 1 LSU beat No. 4 Oklahoma 63-28 in the Peach Bowl playoff semifinal on December 28, 2019, in Atlanta. Joe Burrow threw seven touchdown passes, all in the first half, as LSU led 49-14 at the break.
posts.summary: LSU beat Oklahoma 63-28 in the Dec. 28, 2019 Peach Bowl playoff semifinal as Joe Burrow threw seven first-half TD passes and LSU outgained OU 692-322.

posts.title: Mex the Dog: The Story of OU's Beloved Early Sooner Mascot
posts.question: Who was Mex the Dog, the Oklahoma Sooners mascot?
posts.answer: Mex was a dog found as a pup near the Mexican border in 1914 by Army medic Mott Keys, who later brought him to OU. Mex served as a Sooner mascot into the 1920s, died April 30, 1928, and was buried near Owen Field.
posts.summary: Mex the Dog, found near the Mexican border in 1914, became OU's beloved mascot. He died in April 1928, and OU closed for his funeral near Owen Field.

posts.title: Who Has the Most Passing Yards in OU History? Landry Jones
posts.question: Who is Oklahoma's career passing yards leader?
posts.answer: Landry Jones is Oklahoma's career passing leader with 16,646 yards and 123 touchdown passes as the Sooners' quarterback from 2009 to 2012. That is more than 4,300 yards ahead of No. 2 Baker Mayfield (12,292) through the 2025 season.
posts.summary: Landry Jones holds OU's career passing record with 16,646 yards and 123 TDs, more than 4,300 yards clear of Baker Mayfield. Here is the full top five.

posts.title: Orange Bowl Playoff, Dec. 2018: Alabama 45, Oklahoma 34
posts.question: What was the score when Oklahoma played Alabama in the Orange Bowl playoff semifinal?
posts.answer: Alabama beat Oklahoma 45-34 in the College Football Playoff semifinal at the Orange Bowl on December 29, 2018. The top-ranked Tide led 28-0 early in the second quarter before Kyler Murray led an OU rally.
posts.summary: No. 1 Alabama beat No. 4 Oklahoma 45-34 in the Dec. 29, 2018 Orange Bowl semifinal after leading 28-0, despite 417 total yards from Kyler Murray.

posts.title: George Cumby Joins the College Football Hall of Fame Class of 2026
posts.question: Which Oklahoma Sooner was selected for the College Football Hall of Fame in 2026?
posts.answer: Linebacker George Cumby (OU 1975-79) was named to the College Football Hall of Fame's 2026 class, becoming the 25th former Oklahoma player chosen. His induction is scheduled for Dec. 8, 2026, in Las Vegas.
posts.summary: OU linebacker George Cumby made the College Football Hall of Fame's 2026 class as the 25th Sooner player chosen. Here are his stats, honors and NFL career.

posts.title: Samaje Perine's 427-Yard Game: The FBS Single-Game Rushing Record
posts.question: What is Oklahoma's single-game rushing record?
posts.answer: Samaje Perine ran for 427 yards against Kansas on Nov. 22, 2014, as a true freshman, setting both the Oklahoma and FBS single-game rushing records. Through the 2025 season, no FBS player has topped it.
posts.summary: Samaje Perine ran for 427 yards vs. Kansas on Nov. 22, 2014, as a true freshman, the OU and FBS single-game rushing record that still stands today.

posts.title: 2018 Rose Bowl: Georgia 54, Oklahoma 48 in Double Overtime
posts.question: What was the score of the 2018 Rose Bowl between Oklahoma and Georgia?
posts.answer: Georgia beat Oklahoma 54-48 in double overtime on January 1, 2018, in a College Football Playoff semifinal. It was the first Rose Bowl ever to go to overtime and the highest-scoring Rose Bowl in history.
posts.summary: Georgia beat Oklahoma 54-48 in double OT in the Jan. 1, 2018 Rose Bowl playoff semifinal, the first overtime Rose Bowl and the highest-scoring in its history.

posts.title: Did Troy Aikman Play for Oklahoma? The Hall of Famer's OU Years
posts.question: Did Troy Aikman play college football at Oklahoma before UCLA?
posts.answer: Yes. Troy Aikman, a Henryetta, Oklahoma, product, was a Sooner in 1984 and 1985 before transferring to UCLA. He went No. 1 overall in 1989, won three Super Bowls with Dallas and entered the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2006.
posts.summary: Troy Aikman began his college career at Oklahoma in 1984-85 before UCLA, then won three Super Bowls and reached Canton in 2006. Here is how his OU stint went.

posts.title: Who Is Oklahoma's Career Rushing Leader? Samaje Perine's 4,122 Yards
posts.question: Who is Oklahoma's all-time leading rusher?
posts.answer: Samaje Perine is Oklahoma's career rushing leader with 4,122 yards from 2014 to 2016, just four yards ahead of Billy Sims (4,118). He took the record in the Sugar Bowl against Auburn on Jan. 2, 2017, and it still stands through the 2025 season.
posts.summary: Samaje Perine is OU's career rushing leader with 4,122 yards (2014-16), four yards ahead of Billy Sims. See the top five and how close the race really was.

posts.title: 2014 Sugar Bowl: Trevor Knight and OU Stun Alabama 45-31
posts.question: Who won the 2014 Sugar Bowl between Oklahoma and Alabama?
posts.answer: Oklahoma won, beating No. 3 Alabama 45-31 on January 2, 2014, in New Orleans. Freshman quarterback Trevor Knight threw for 348 yards and four touchdowns and was named MVP.
posts.summary: No. 11 Oklahoma upset No. 3 Alabama 45-31 in the Jan. 2, 2014 Sugar Bowl as freshman QB Trevor Knight threw four TDs and set a Sugar Bowl completions record.

posts.title: Dede Westbrook: OU's First Biletnikoff Award Winner in 2016
posts.question: Who was the first Oklahoma player to win the Biletnikoff Award?
posts.answer: Wide receiver Dede Westbrook was the first Sooner to win the Biletnikoff Award, earning it on Dec. 8, 2016, as college football's top receiver. He had 1,465 receiving yards and a school-record 16 touchdown catches at the time.
posts.summary: Dede Westbrook became OU's first Biletnikoff Award winner in 2016 after a season of 1,465 receiving yards and a school-record 16 TD catches. Here's the story.

posts.title: Oklahoma Sooners All-Time Bowl Record: 31-26-1 in 58 Games
posts.question: What is Oklahoma's all-time bowl record?
posts.answer: Oklahoma's all-time bowl record is 31-26-1 in 58 bowl games, a mark unchanged since the 2024 Armed Forces Bowl because OU's 2025 playoff game in Norman is not counted as a bowl. Its 58 appearances ranked fourth nationally entering that 2024 bowl.
posts.summary: Oklahoma is 31-26-1 in 58 bowl games, fourth nationally in appearances. Here are its New Year's Six totals, record bowl streak and playoff results.

posts.title: 2007 Fiesta Bowl: How Boise State Beat OU 43-42 in Overtime
posts.question: What happened in the 2007 Fiesta Bowl between Oklahoma and Boise State?
posts.answer: Unbeaten Boise State beat Oklahoma 43-42 in overtime on January 1, 2007, tying the game with a hook-and-lateral in the final seconds and winning on a Statue of Liberty two-point conversion.
posts.summary: Boise State beat Oklahoma 43-42 in OT at the Jan. 1, 2007 Fiesta Bowl using a hook-and-lateral, a halfback pass and the Statue of Liberty play to finish.

posts.title: Rocky Calmus Wins the 2001 Butkus Award for Oklahoma
posts.question: When did Rocky Calmus win the Butkus Award?
posts.answer: Rocky Calmus won the Butkus Award on Dec. 7, 2001, as the nation's best linebacker. It was Oklahoma's third Butkus Award and the first since Brian Bosworth won it in 1985 and 1986.
posts.summary: Rocky Calmus won the 2001 Butkus Award, OU's first since Brian Bosworth, after a 117-tackle senior year. Dick Butkus himself handed him the trophy in Orlando.

posts.title: Cotton Bowl, Dec. 2020: OU Routs Florida 55-20 With 684 Yards
posts.question: Who won the Cotton Bowl between Oklahoma and Florida in December 2020?
posts.answer: Oklahoma beat Florida 55-20 in the Cotton Bowl on December 30, 2020, in Arlington, Texas. The Sooners' 55 points and 684 total yards were the most they had ever produced in a bowl game.
posts.summary: Oklahoma beat Florida 55-20 in the Dec. 30, 2020 Cotton Bowl, rushing for 435 yards and setting school bowl highs for points and total yards (684).

posts.title: 1954 Orange Bowl: How OU Shut Out No. 1 Maryland 7-0
posts.question: Did Oklahoma beat No. 1 Maryland in the 1954 Orange Bowl?
posts.answer: Yes. On January 1, 1954, Bud Wilkinson's fourth-ranked Sooners beat top-ranked, unbeaten Maryland 7-0 in the Orange Bowl, the first time Maryland had been shut out in 51 games.
posts.summary: On Jan. 1, 1954, Bud Wilkinson's No. 4 Oklahoma shut out No. 1 Maryland 7-0 in the Orange Bowl, ending the Terrapins' 51-game run without being shut out.

posts.title: Teddy Lehman's 2003 Bednarik and Butkus Award Sweep
posts.question: Which Oklahoma linebacker won the Bednarik Award and Butkus Award in 2003?
posts.answer: Linebacker Teddy Lehman won the Chuck Bednarik Award on Dec. 11, 2003, and the Butkus Award the next night. He was OU's first Bednarik winner and gave the Sooners a fourth Butkus Award.
posts.summary: Teddy Lehman won the 2003 Bednarik Award and Butkus Award on back-to-back nights, OU's first Bednarik and its fourth Butkus, the most of any program then.

posts.title: OU's First College Football Playoff Game: 2015 Orange Bowl vs Clemson
posts.question: When did Oklahoma make its first College Football Playoff appearance?
posts.answer: Oklahoma's first College Football Playoff game was the Orange Bowl semifinal on December 31, 2015. The No. 4 Sooners led No. 1 Clemson 17-16 at halftime but lost 37-17.
posts.summary: OU's first College Football Playoff game was the Dec. 31, 2015 Orange Bowl semifinal. The Sooners led Clemson 17-16 at the half before falling 37-17.

posts.title: Has Oklahoma Ever Beaten Notre Dame? OU's Two Wins, 1956 and 2013
posts.question: How many times has Oklahoma beaten Notre Dame in football?
posts.answer: Oklahoma has beaten Notre Dame twice in 11 meetings: 40-0 in South Bend on October 27, 1956, and 35-21 in South Bend on September 28, 2013. Notre Dame won the other nine games on the field, though its 2012 win was later vacated by the NCAA.
posts.summary: OU has beaten Notre Dame only twice: 40-0 in South Bend in 1956 and 35-21 there in 2013. Here's the story of both wins in a series the Irish dominate.

posts.title: Derrick Strait: OU's 2003 Nagurski and Thorpe Winner
posts.question: Which Oklahoma cornerback won the Nagurski Trophy and Thorpe Award in 2003?
posts.answer: Cornerback Derrick Strait won both the 2003 Bronko Nagurski Trophy and the 2003 Jim Thorpe Award. He was the second OU defensive back in three seasons to win the Nagurski, after Roy Williams in 2001.
posts.summary: Derrick Strait swept the 2003 Nagurski Trophy and Thorpe Award at OU, setting school records for pass breakups, career starts and interception return yards.

posts.title: OU's First Rose Bowl: 34-14 Over Washington State in 2003
posts.question: When did Oklahoma first play in the Rose Bowl?
posts.answer: Oklahoma's first Rose Bowl was on January 1, 2003, when Bob Stoops' No. 8 Sooners beat No. 7 Washington State 34-14 in Pasadena. Quarterback Nate Hybl was named the game's MVP.
posts.summary: Oklahoma's first Rose Bowl came on Jan. 1, 2003, a 34-14 win over Washington State. Nate Hybl was MVP and OU's defense held the Cougars to 4 rushing yards.

posts.title: OU 38, No. 1 Missouri 17: The 2007 Big 12 Championship Game
posts.question: When did Oklahoma beat No. 1 Missouri in the Big 12 Championship Game?
posts.answer: Oklahoma beat top-ranked Missouri 38-17 in the Big 12 Championship Game on December 1, 2007, at the Alamodome in San Antonio. The Sooners pulled away after a 14-14 halftime tie and ended Missouri's national title hopes.
posts.summary: OU beat No. 1 Missouri 38-17 in the 2007 Big 12 Championship in San Antonio. It stood as the Sooners' last win over a No. 1 team until 2026.

posts.title: Roy Williams' 2001 Nagurski and Thorpe Award Double at OU
posts.question: What awards did Roy Williams win at Oklahoma in 2001?
posts.answer: In 2001 Oklahoma safety Roy Williams won both the Bronko Nagurski Trophy as the nation's top defender and the Jim Thorpe Award as the top defensive back. He was the first player ever to win both in the same year.
posts.summary: In 2001 OU safety Roy Williams became the first player to win the Nagurski Trophy and Thorpe Award in one season, the year of his famous Superman play vs Texas.

posts.title: CeeDee Lamb's Record 2023: 135 Catches and Cowboys History
posts.question: What Dallas Cowboys records does former Sooner CeeDee Lamb hold?
posts.answer: CeeDee Lamb (OU 2017-19) holds the Cowboys' single-season records for receptions (135) and receiving yards (1,749), both set in 2023, when he also became the first player in franchise history to lead the NFL in catches.
posts.summary: Ex-Sooner CeeDee Lamb set Cowboys single-season records with 135 catches and 1,749 yards in 2023, breaking Michael Irvin's marks. His OU and NFL story.

posts.title: What Was OU's First Bowl Game? The 1939 Orange Bowl
posts.question: What was Oklahoma's first bowl game?
posts.answer: Oklahoma's first bowl game was the Orange Bowl in Miami on January 2, 1939, where unbeaten Tennessee shut out the unbeaten Sooners 17-0. Tom Stidham was OU's head coach.
posts.summary: Oklahoma's first bowl game was the January 2, 1939 Orange Bowl, a 17-0 loss to Tennessee in a matchup of 10-0 teams. Here is how the trip to Miami came about.

posts.title: Kansas State 35, Oklahoma 7: The 2003 Big 12 Title Game Upset
posts.question: Who beat undefeated No. 1 Oklahoma in the 2003 Big 12 Championship Game?
posts.answer: No. 13 Kansas State beat No. 1 Oklahoma 35-7 in the Big 12 Championship Game on December 6, 2003, at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City. OU still finished No. 1 in the BCS standings and played LSU for the national title.
posts.summary: Kansas State stunned unbeaten No. 1 Oklahoma 35-7 in the 2003 Big 12 Championship. Darren Sproles ran for 235 yards, yet OU still reached the BCS title game.

posts.title: Rickey Dixon: First Sooner to Win the Jim Thorpe Award
posts.question: Who was the first Oklahoma player to win the Jim Thorpe Award?
posts.answer: Safety Rickey Dixon was the first Sooner to win the Jim Thorpe Award, sharing the 1987 honor with Miami's Bennie Blades. He set OU's single-season record with nine interceptions that year.
posts.summary: Rickey Dixon became the first Sooner to win the Jim Thorpe Award in 1987, sharing it with Miami's Bennie Blades after a school-record nine interceptions.

posts.title: Trent Williams' 12 Pro Bowls: An OU Tackle Among the NFL's Best
posts.question: How many Pro Bowls has former Oklahoma tackle Trent Williams made?
posts.answer: Twelve. Trent Williams (OU 2006-09), the No. 4 pick in the 2010 NFL Draft, earned his 12th Pro Bowl selection for the 2025 season, making him one of only four offensive linemen in NFL history with 12 or more.
posts.summary: Former Sooner Trent Williams has 12 Pro Bowl nods, joining Bruce Matthews, Randall McDaniel and Will Shields among the NFL's most honored offensive linemen.

posts.title: 2008 Sooners: Five Straight 60-Point Games and a Scoring Record
posts.question: Which Oklahoma team scored 60 points in five straight games?
posts.answer: The 2008 Oklahoma Sooners scored at least 60 points in five consecutive games, capped by a 62-21 win over Missouri in the Big 12 Championship Game. That team scored 716 points, then the Division I single-season record.
posts.summary: The 2008 Sooners scored 60+ in five straight games, capped by a 62-21 Big 12 title win over Missouri, and set a then-record 716 points in a season.

posts.title: 2018 Big 12 Title Game: How OU Avenged Its Loss to Texas, 39-27
posts.question: Who won the 2018 Big 12 Championship Game between Oklahoma and Texas?
posts.answer: Oklahoma won the 2018 Big 12 Championship Game 39-27 over Texas on December 1, 2018, in Arlington, avenging a 48-45 regular-season loss. It was OU's fourth straight Big 12 title and 12th overall.
posts.summary: OU beat Texas 39-27 in the 2018 Big 12 Championship, avenging a 48-45 loss in Dallas. Kyler Murray threw for 379 yards as OU won a fourth straight title.

posts.title: Tommie Harris: OU's 2003 Lombardi Award Winner
posts.question: Which Oklahoma defensive tackle won the Lombardi Award in 2003?
posts.answer: Tommie Harris won the 2003 Lombardi Award as the nation's top lineman, becoming the third Sooner to win it. The Killeen, Texas, junior had been the runner-up in 2002 and returned to claim the honor.
posts.summary: Tommie Harris won the 2003 Lombardi Award, the third Sooner to do so, after finishing runner-up in 2002. See his 2003 stats and how his NFL career unfolded.

posts.title: Lane Johnson: From OU Tight End to Two-Time Super Bowl Champion
posts.question: Which former Oklahoma Sooner won two Super Bowls with the Philadelphia Eagles?
posts.answer: Right tackle Lane Johnson (OU 2009-12) won Super Bowl LII and Super Bowl LIX with Philadelphia. The 2013 No. 4 overall pick made six Pro Bowls over 14 seasons, all with the Eagles, before announcing his retirement in October 2026.
posts.summary: Lane Johnson went from Kilgore College QB and OU tight end to a two-time Super Bowl champion right tackle for the Eagles. Here is his unlikely path.

posts.title: OU vs Nebraska Rivalry History and All-Time Series Record
posts.question: What is Oklahoma's all-time football record against Nebraska?
posts.answer: Oklahoma leads Nebraska 47-38-3 through the schools' 2022 meeting, a 49-14 OU win in Lincoln. The rivalry began in 1912, and the teams are scheduled to meet again in 2029 and 2030.
posts.summary: OU leads Nebraska 47-38-3 through 2022. From the 1912 opener and Nebraska's 1959 upset to the 2021-22 renewal, here's the Big Red rivalry's history.

posts.title: OU 63, Texas 14: Quentin Griffin's Six-TD Day in the 2000 Rout
posts.question: What happened in the 2000 Oklahoma vs Texas game when OU won 63-14?
posts.answer: On October 7, 2000, No. 10 Oklahoma beat No. 11 Texas 63-14 in Dallas. Quentin Griffin ran for a school-record six touchdowns, OU led 42-0 in the second quarter, and Texas finished with minus-7 rushing yards.
posts.summary: OU crushed Texas 63-14 in 2000 as Quentin Griffin ran for a school-record six touchdowns and the Longhorns finished with minus-7 rushing yards.

posts.title: Tony Casillas and His 1985 Lombardi Award at Oklahoma
posts.question: Did Tony Casillas win the Lombardi Award at Oklahoma?
posts.answer: Yes. Nose guard Tony Casillas won the Lombardi Award in 1985, becoming the second Sooner to win it, and helped lead Oklahoma to the national championship that season. He was a consensus All-American in 1984 and 1985.
posts.summary: Tony Casillas won the 1985 Lombardi Award as OU's nose guard, the second Sooner to win it, then went No. 2 overall in the NFL draft and won two Super Bowls.

posts.title: Gerald McCoy's NFL Career: Six Straight Pro Bowls in Tampa Bay
posts.question: How many Pro Bowls did Gerald McCoy make after leaving Oklahoma?
posts.answer: Six. Gerald McCoy (OU 2006-09), the No. 3 pick in the 2010 NFL Draft, made six consecutive Pro Bowls with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers from 2012 to 2017 and retired in April 2023 with 59.5 career sacks.
posts.summary: Oklahoma City's Gerald McCoy went No. 3 overall in 2010 and made six straight Pro Bowls for Tampa Bay. Here is the former Sooner's NFL career by the numbers.

posts.title: Bedlam Series Record: OU vs Oklahoma State From 1904 to 2023
posts.question: What is Oklahoma's all-time record against Oklahoma State, and why did Bedlam stop?
posts.answer: Oklahoma leads the Bedlam football series 91-20-7. The rivalry began with a 75-0 OU win in Guthrie in 1904, and the annual series went on hold after Oklahoma State's 27-24 win in 2023, when OU left the Big 12 for the SEC.
posts.summary: OU leads Bedlam 91-20-7 after the 2023 game. From a 75-0 win in 1904 Guthrie to OSU's 27-24 finale, here's how the annual rivalry went on hold.

posts.title: What Is the Golden Hat? The OU-Texas Red River Trophy Explained
posts.question: What is the Golden Hat trophy in the Oklahoma vs Texas game?
posts.answer: The Golden Hat is the trophy awarded on the field to the winner of the Oklahoma-Texas game: a replica of a ten-gallon cowboy hat tied to the State Fair of Texas. It began as a bronze hat, commonly dated to 1941, and turned gold after a 1970s makeover.
posts.summary: The Golden Hat is the Red River Rivalry's on-field trophy, a ten-gallon hat tied to the State Fair of Texas. Learn why it started as the Bronze Hat.

posts.title: Jammal Brown's 2004 Outland Trophy: OU's Fifth Winner
posts.question: When did Jammal Brown win the Outland Trophy for Oklahoma?
posts.answer: Offensive tackle Jammal Brown won the Outland Trophy in December 2004, becoming the fifth Oklahoma player to win it and the first since Greg Roberts in 1978. He did not allow a sack all season.
posts.summary: Jammal Brown won the 2004 Outland Trophy, OU's fifth and its first since 1978, after a season in which the Sooner tackle allowed no sacks, hurries or QB hits.

posts.title: Tommie Harris: OU's Lombardi Winner and a Three-Time Pro Bowler
posts.question: How many Pro Bowls did former Oklahoma defensive tackle Tommie Harris make with the Chicago Bears?
posts.answer: Three. Tommie Harris (OU 2001-03), the 2003 Lombardi Award winner, went 14th overall to the Chicago Bears in 2004 and made three straight Pro Bowls, in 2005, 2006 and 2007.
posts.summary: Sooner DT Tommie Harris won the 2003 Lombardi Award, went 14th overall to Chicago and made three straight Pro Bowls. A look at his OU and NFL career highlights.

posts.title: OU's Biggest Win Over Texas: The 65-13 Red River Rout of 2003
posts.question: What is Oklahoma's largest margin of victory over Texas?
posts.answer: Oklahoma's largest win over Texas is 65-13 on October 11, 2003, in Dallas. The 52-point margin is the biggest in the Red River series, and the 65 points are the most OU has scored against the Longhorns.
posts.summary: OU's 65-13 win over Texas on Oct. 11, 2003, is the largest margin in Red River Rivalry history. Relive the six-turnover, 290-yard passing blowout.

posts.title: When Was the First Red River Rivalry Game? OU vs Texas in 1900
posts.question: When did Oklahoma and Texas first play football, and who won?
posts.answer: Oklahoma and Texas first met on October 10, 1900, in Austin, and Texas won 28-2. The Sooners did not beat the Longhorns until their eighth meeting, a 2-0 win in Oklahoma City in 1905.
posts.summary: The Red River Rivalry began October 10, 1900, in Austin with a 28-2 Texas win. See how OU got its first win in 1905 and how the game landed in Dallas.

posts.title: Greg Roberts: OU Guard Who Won the 1978 Outland Trophy
posts.question: Which Oklahoma lineman won the Outland Trophy in 1978?
posts.answer: Guard Greg Roberts won the 1978 Outland Trophy, becoming the fourth Sooner to earn the award for the nation's best interior lineman. He was a consensus All-American that year while blocking for Heisman winner Billy Sims.
posts.summary: Greg Roberts won the 1978 Outland Trophy as OU's right guard, the fourth Sooner to win it, opening holes for Billy Sims and the nation's top rushing team.

posts.title: Roy Williams: From OU's Superman to Five Straight Pro Bowls
posts.question: How many Pro Bowls did former Oklahoma safety Roy Williams make in the NFL?
posts.answer: Five. Roy Williams (OU 1999-2001), the No. 8 overall pick of the Dallas Cowboys in 2002, made five consecutive Pro Bowls for the 2003 through 2007 seasons and was a first-team All-Pro in 2003.
posts.summary: Ex-Sooner safety Roy Williams went No. 8 overall in 2002 and made five straight Pro Bowls with Dallas. His OU awards, NFL career and Hall of Fame honors.

posts.title: OU vs Texas All-Time Record: Red River Series Through 2026
posts.question: What is Oklahoma's all-time record against Texas in football?
posts.answer: Through the 2026 meeting, Texas leads the Red River Rivalry 65-52-5. Oklahoma won the 2026 game 27-24 over No. 1 Texas on Tate Sandell's 47-yard field goal on the final play.
posts.summary: Through the 2026 game, Texas leads OU 65-52-5 in the Red River Rivalry. Here's how the Sooners' 27-24 upset of No. 1 Texas changed the series record.

posts.title: When Did Oklahoma Join the SEC? The Sooners' 2024 Move
posts.question: When did the Oklahoma Sooners officially join the SEC?
posts.answer: Oklahoma officially became a member of the Southeastern Conference on July 1, 2024, joining alongside Texas and growing the SEC to 16 schools. The Sooners played their first SEC game on Sept. 21, 2024, against Tennessee in Norman.
posts.summary: Oklahoma officially joined the SEC on July 1, 2024, alongside Texas, after leaving the Big 12 a year early. Here is the timeline and the first SEC game.

posts.title: J.D. Roberts: OU Guard Who Won the 1953 Outland Trophy
posts.question: Which Oklahoma guard won the Outland Trophy in 1953?
posts.answer: J.D. Roberts, a two-way guard for Bud Wilkinson, won the 1953 Outland Trophy as the nation's top interior lineman. He was a consensus All-American that season and later became head coach of the New Orleans Saints.
posts.summary: J.D. Roberts won the 1953 Outland Trophy as a two-way guard at Oklahoma, helped start the 47-game streak, and later coached the New Orleans Saints in the NFL.

posts.title: Joe Washington in the NFL: 1979 Catch Leader and Super Bowl Champ
posts.question: What did Joe Washington accomplish in the NFL after Oklahoma?
posts.answer: Joe Washington (OU 1972-75), the No. 4 overall pick in 1976, led the NFL with 82 receptions for the Colts in 1979, made the Pro Bowl that season and won Super Bowl XVII with Washington after the 1982 season.
posts.summary: OU legend Joe Washington led the NFL with 82 catches in 1979, made the Pro Bowl and won Super Bowl XVII. A look at the former Sooner's nine-season NFL career.

posts.title: Which Oklahoma Coaches Are in the College Football Hall of Fame?
posts.question: Which Oklahoma Sooners head football coaches are in the College Football Hall of Fame?
posts.answer: Six former Oklahoma head coaches are enshrined as coaches: Bennie Owen (1951), Lawrence "Biff" Jones (1954), Bud Wilkinson (1969), Jim Tatum (1984), Barry Switzer (2001) and Bob Stoops (2021 class). Gomer Jones, OU's coach in 1964-65, is also in, but as a player.
posts.summary: Six OU head coaches are in the College Football Hall of Fame as coaches: Owen, Biff Jones, Wilkinson, Tatum, Switzer and Stoops. Gomer Jones got in as a player.

posts.title: When Did Oklahoma Hire Brent Venables as Head Coach?
posts.question: When did Oklahoma hire Brent Venables, and what was his background?
posts.answer: Oklahoma hired Brent Venables as head coach on Dec. 5, 2021, to replace Lincoln Riley. A Sooner assistant from 1999 to 2011, he came from Clemson, where he had been defensive coordinator for 10 seasons, and it was his first head coaching job.
posts.summary: OU hired Brent Venables on Dec. 5, 2021, bringing home a former Sooner defensive coordinator from Clemson for his first head coaching job. Details here.

posts.title: Jim Weatherall: OU's First Outland Trophy Winner in 1951
posts.question: Who was the first Oklahoma Sooner to win the Outland Trophy?
posts.answer: Tackle Jim Weatherall was the first Oklahoma player to win the Outland Trophy, taking the award as the nation's top interior lineman in 1951. He was a consensus All-American in 1950 and a unanimous All-American in 1951.
posts.summary: Jim Weatherall became the first Sooner to win the Outland Trophy in 1951. Learn how the two-time All-America tackle and kicker anchored Bud Wilkinson's OU.

posts.title: Greg Pruitt's NFL Career: Five Pro Bowls and a Super Bowl Ring
posts.question: What did Greg Pruitt do in the NFL after playing at Oklahoma?
posts.answer: Greg Pruitt (OU 1970-72) was a 1973 second-round pick of the Cleveland Browns who made five Pro Bowls, four with Cleveland and one with the Raiders, and won Super Bowl XVIII with the Los Angeles Raiders.
posts.summary: Former Sooner Greg Pruitt made five Pro Bowls with the Browns and Raiders and won Super Bowl XVIII. A look at the NFL career of OU's two-time All-American.

posts.title: How Many Big 12 Titles Did Lincoln Riley Win at Oklahoma?
posts.question: How many Big 12 championships did Lincoln Riley win as Oklahoma's head coach?
posts.answer: Four. Lincoln Riley won the Big 12 championship in each of his first four seasons as OU's head coach, 2017 through 2020, and led the Sooners to the College Football Playoff in 2017, 2018 and 2019.
posts.summary: Lincoln Riley won four straight Big 12 titles at Oklahoma from 2017 to 2020 and went 55-10, the best winning percentage of any Sooner head coach.

posts.title: Who Coached OU Between Gary Gibbs and Bob Stoops? (1995-1998)
posts.question: Who coached Oklahoma football between Gary Gibbs and Bob Stoops?
posts.answer: Two coaches: Howard Schnellenberger led Oklahoma for the 1995 season and went 5-5-1, and former Sooner nose guard John Blake coached from 1996 through 1998 and went 12-22. Bob Stoops was hired on Dec. 1, 1998.
posts.summary: Between Gary Gibbs and Bob Stoops, Oklahoma was coached by Howard Schnellenberger in 1995 and John Blake from 1996 to 1998. Here are the facts.

posts.title: Gomer Jones: The Man Who Followed Bud Wilkinson at Oklahoma
posts.question: Who replaced Bud Wilkinson as Oklahoma's head football coach?
posts.answer: Gomer Jones, Bud Wilkinson's longtime line coach, succeeded him in 1964 and coached two seasons, going 9-11-1. Jones was also OU's athletic director from 1964 until his death in 1971.
posts.summary: Gomer Jones followed Bud Wilkinson as OU coach in 1964, went 9-11-1 in two seasons, and served as athletic director until 1971. Here is his story.

posts.title: Oklahoma's 2010 NFL Draft: Three Sooners in the First Four Picks
posts.question: Which school had three players taken in the first four picks of the 2010 NFL Draft?
posts.answer: Oklahoma. In 2010 Sam Bradford went No. 1 to St. Louis, Gerald McCoy No. 3 to Tampa Bay and Trent Williams No. 4 to Washington, making OU the first school in NFL Draft history with three of the first four picks.
posts.summary: In 2010 Oklahoma became the first school with three of the NFL Draft's first four picks: Sam Bradford, Gerald McCoy and Trent Williams. Here is the story.

posts.title: Bob Stoops: Hired in 1998, OU's All-Time Wins Leader
posts.question: When was Bob Stoops hired at Oklahoma and how many games did he win?
posts.answer: Oklahoma hired Bob Stoops on Dec. 1, 1998, from Florida, where he was defensive coordinator. He went 190-48 from 1999 to 2016, the most wins in OU history, and passed Barry Switzer's 157 on Nov. 23, 2013, at Kansas State.
posts.summary: OU hired Bob Stoops on Dec. 1, 1998. He went 190-48 over 18 seasons, passing Barry Switzer in 2013 to become the program's all-time wins leader.

posts.title: When Did Oklahoma Switch to the Wishbone? The 1970 Gamble
posts.question: When did Oklahoma switch to the wishbone offense, and who made the call?
posts.answer: Oklahoma switched to the wishbone midway through the 1970 season under head coach Chuck Fairbanks, debuting it against Texas on Oct. 10, 1970. Offensive coordinator Barry Switzer persuaded Fairbanks to make the change after an early loss to Oregon State.
posts.summary: OU switched to the wishbone in October 1970 under Chuck Fairbanks, debuting it against Texas after Barry Switzer pushed for the change. Here is how.

posts.title: Bud Wilkinson's Hiring at OU and His 145-29-4 Career Record
posts.question: When did Bud Wilkinson become Oklahoma's head coach and what was his overall record?
posts.answer: Bud Wilkinson became Oklahoma's head coach and athletic director in 1947, at age 31, after one season as Jim Tatum's assistant. In 17 seasons through 1963 he went 145-29-4, an .826 winning percentage, and won conference titles in 14 of them.
posts.summary: Bud Wilkinson took over OU in 1947 at age 31 and went 145-29-4 over 17 seasons, winning league titles in 14 of them. Here is how the hire happened.

posts.title: Every Oklahoma Sooner Picked No. 1 Overall in the NFL Draft
posts.question: How many Oklahoma Sooners have been the No. 1 overall pick in the NFL Draft?
posts.answer: Five Sooners have gone first overall: Lee Roy Selmon (1976), Billy Sims (1980), Sam Bradford (2010), Baker Mayfield (2018) and Kyler Murray (2019). That ties Oklahoma with Georgia and Notre Dame for second-most, one behind USC.
posts.summary: Five Sooners have gone No. 1 overall in the NFL Draft, from Lee Roy Selmon in 1976 to Kyler Murray in 2019. See the full list with teams and OU years.

posts.title: Barry Switzer's Career Record at Oklahoma: 157-29-4 and .837
posts.question: What was Barry Switzer's career record and winning percentage at Oklahoma?
posts.answer: Barry Switzer went 157-29-4 in 16 seasons as Oklahoma's head coach (1973-1988), an .837 winning percentage, with 12 Big Eight titles and three national championships. His 157 wins were the school record until Bob Stoops passed him in 2013.
posts.summary: Barry Switzer went 157-29-4 (.837) in 16 seasons at OU from 1973 to 1988, winning 12 Big Eight titles. Here are the numbers behind his record.

posts.title: Jim Tatum's Only Season at Oklahoma: The 1946 Sooners
posts.question: Who coached Oklahoma football in 1946, right before Bud Wilkinson?
posts.answer: Jim Tatum coached Oklahoma for one season, 1946, going 8-3, sharing the Big Six title and beating NC State 34-13 in the Gator Bowl on Jan. 1, 1947. He then left for Maryland, and his assistant Bud Wilkinson took over.
posts.summary: Jim Tatum coached OU for just the 1946 season, went 8-3, shared the Big Six title and won the Gator Bowl before leaving for Maryland and Bud Wilkinson.

posts.title: Bennie Owen: OU's Longest-Tenured Football Coach (1905-1926)
posts.question: How long did Bennie Owen coach Oklahoma football and what was his record?
posts.answer: Bennie Owen coached the Oklahoma Sooners from 1905 through 1926, the longest tenure of any OU head coach, and went 122-54-16. His 1911, 1915 and 1918 teams went unbeaten, and Owen Field carries his name.
posts.summary: Bennie Owen coached Oklahoma from 1905 to 1926, went 122-54-16, posted three unbeaten seasons and gave his name to Owen Field. Here is his story.

posts.title: Bob Kalsu: The OU All-American Who Gave His Life in Vietnam
posts.question: Which former OU football player was killed in the Vietnam War?
posts.answer: Bob Kalsu, OU's All-America tackle in 1967, left the Buffalo Bills to serve in the Army and was killed in Vietnam on July 21, 1970.
posts.summary: Bob Kalsu, OU's 1967 All-America tackle, left the Buffalo Bills for Army service and was killed at Firebase Ripcord in Vietnam on July 21, 1970.

posts.title: Adrian Peterson's 2004 Freshman Season: 1,925 Yards at OU
posts.question: How many yards did Adrian Peterson rush for as a freshman at Oklahoma?
posts.answer: Adrian Peterson ran for 1,925 yards on a nation-leading 339 carries as a true freshman in 2004, an NCAA freshman record, and finished second in the Heisman voting.
posts.summary: Adrian Peterson ran for an NCAA freshman record 1,925 yards in 2004 and became the first freshman to finish as Heisman runner-up, behind USC's Matt Leinart.

posts.title: Darrell Royal: The Sooner Who Became a Texas Coaching Legend
posts.question: Did Texas coach Darrell Royal play football at Oklahoma?
posts.answer: Darrell Royal, an OU quarterback and defensive back from 1946 to 1949, coached Texas from 1957 to 1976 and won national titles in 1963, 1969 and 1970.
posts.summary: Darrell Royal starred at OU from 1946 to 1949, then coached Texas from 1957 to 1976, won three national titles and entered the College Football Hall of Fame.

posts.title: Brian Bosworth: OU's Two-Time Butkus Award Linebacker
posts.question: Who won the first two Butkus Awards?
posts.answer: Oklahoma linebacker Brian Bosworth won the first two Butkus Awards, in 1985 and 1986, and remains the award's only two-time college winner.
posts.summary: Brian Bosworth won the first two Butkus Awards in 1985 and 1986, led OU in tackles three straight years and helped win the 1985 national title.

posts.title: Prentice Gautt: OU Pioneer Who Became a Conference Executive
posts.question: What did Prentice Gautt, OU's first Black football player, do after football?
posts.answer: Prentice Gautt, OU's first Black football player (1956-59), earned a Ph.D. in counseling psychology and became an associate commissioner of the Big Eight and later the Big 12.
posts.summary: Prentice Gautt, OU's first Black football player (1956-59), earned a Ph.D. in counseling psychology and became a Big Eight and Big 12 associate commissioner.

posts.title: Lee Roy Selmon and the Selmon Brothers of Eufaula, Oklahoma
posts.question: Which three Selmon brothers played football at Oklahoma?
posts.answer: Lucious, Dewey and Lee Roy Selmon, all from Eufaula, Oklahoma, played for the Sooners. Lee Roy, the youngest, won the Outland Trophy and Lombardi Award in 1975 and reached the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
posts.summary: Lucious, Dewey and Lee Roy Selmon of Eufaula all starred at OU. Lee Roy won the 1975 Outland and Lombardi and became the first player Tampa Bay ever drafted.

posts.title: Lee Roy Selmon: OU Legend Who Became USF's Athletic Director
posts.question: What did Lee Roy Selmon do after his NFL career?
posts.answer: Lee Roy Selmon, an OU defensive lineman from 1972 to 1975, became USF's athletic director in 2001 and opened Lee Roy Selmon's restaurant in Tampa in 2000.
posts.summary: Lee Roy Selmon (OU 1972-75) became a Pro Football Hall of Famer, then served as USF's athletic director and opened a namesake restaurant in Tampa in 2000.

posts.title: Kyler Murray: 2018 Heisman Winner and First-Round MLB Pick
posts.question: Did Kyler Murray get drafted in baseball before winning the Heisman?
posts.answer: Yes. The Oakland Athletics took Kyler Murray ninth overall in the June 2018 MLB draft. He won the Heisman that December and chose football in February 2019, going No. 1 to Arizona.
posts.summary: Kyler Murray was a top-10 MLB draft pick by Oakland in 2018, then won the Heisman at OU and went No. 1 overall in the 2019 NFL draft to the Cardinals.

posts.title: Spencer Tillman: From OU Captain to College Football Broadcaster
posts.question: Which former OU running back became a CBS and Fox college football analyst?
posts.answer: Spencer Tillman, an OU running back from 1983 to 1986, became a broadcaster and was CBS's lead college football studio analyst from 1999 to 2014 before joining Fox Sports.
posts.summary: Spencer Tillman, a captain on OU's 1985 title team, became a TV sportscaster and spent 16 years as CBS's lead college football studio analyst, then joined Fox.

posts.title: Baker Mayfield: From Walk-On to the 2017 Heisman Trophy
posts.question: Was Baker Mayfield a walk-on before winning the Heisman?
posts.answer: Yes. Baker Mayfield walked on at Texas Tech in 2013 and again at Oklahoma, and in 2017 he became the first Heisman winner since scholarships began in the 1950s to start his college career as a walk-on.
posts.summary: Baker Mayfield walked on at Texas Tech and then OU, set an NCAA passer rating record and won the 2017 Heisman before going No. 1 in the 2018 NFL draft.

posts.title: Keith Jackson's P.A.R.K.: An OU Tight End's Gift to Little Rock
posts.question: What nonprofit did former OU tight end Keith Jackson start?
posts.answer: Keith Jackson, OU's All-America tight end from 1984 to 1987, founded P.A.R.K. (Positive Atmosphere Reaches Kids), a Little Rock after-school nonprofit, in 1993.
posts.summary: All-American tight end Keith Jackson (OU 1984-87) founded P.A.R.K., a Little Rock nonprofit that helps at-risk students stay in school and reach college.

posts.title: Why It's Called Owen Field: History of Oklahoma Memorial Stadium
posts.question: Why is Oklahoma's football field called Owen Field?
posts.answer: The playing surface is named for Bennie Owen, OU's coach from 1905 to 1926, who helped raise money for the stadium. The stadium's Memorial name honors university people who died in World War I.
posts.summary: Owen Field honors coach Bennie Owen, and Oklahoma Memorial Stadium honors World War I dead. A short history of the Sooners' home from 1923 to its record crowd.

posts.title: 2008 Oklahoma Offense: 716 Points and Five Straight 60-Point Games
posts.question: Which Oklahoma team scored the most points in a college football season?
posts.answer: The 2008 Sooners scored 716 points, then the NCAA Division I single-season record, and became the first team since Tulsa in 1919 to score 60 or more points in five straight games.
posts.summary: Oklahoma's 2008 offense scored 716 points and hit 60 in five straight games, led by Heisman winner Sam Bradford. Here's the record-setting run, game by game.

posts.title: Sam Bradford's 2008 Heisman: 50 TD Passes and a Close Vote
posts.question: How many touchdowns did Sam Bradford throw in his 2008 Heisman season?
posts.answer: Sam Bradford threw 50 touchdown passes for 4,720 yards in 2008, counting the national title game, and won that year's Heisman Trophy as a redshirt sophomore.
posts.summary: Oklahoma City's Sam Bradford threw 50 TD passes in 2008 and won the Heisman over Colt McCoy and Tim Tebow, then went No. 1 overall in the 2010 NFL draft.

posts.title: Steve Owens: Heisman Winner, Norman Businessman and OU AD
posts.question: Was Heisman winner Steve Owens ever OU's athletic director?
posts.answer: Steve Owens, OU's 1969 Heisman winner, served as the university's athletic director from August 1996 to March 1998 after building several businesses in Norman.
posts.summary: 1969 Heisman winner Steve Owens (OU 1967-69) built businesses in Norman, helped found the Oklahoma Sports Hall of Fame and served as OU athletic director.

posts.title: Oklahoma 13, Florida State 2: The 2000 National Championship Game
posts.question: What was the score when Oklahoma won the 2000 national championship?
posts.answer: Oklahoma beat Florida State 13-2 in the Orange Bowl on Jan. 3, 2001, finishing 13-0 and winning the BCS national title in Bob Stoops' second season as head coach.
posts.summary: Oklahoma beat Florida State 13-2 in the Jan. 3, 2001 Orange Bowl to finish 13-0 and win the BCS title. Here is how the Sooners defense shut down the Seminoles.

posts.title: How Many National Championships Has Oklahoma Football Won? Seven
posts.question: How many national championships has Oklahoma football won?
posts.answer: Oklahoma claims seven national championships: 1950, 1955 and 1956 under Bud Wilkinson; 1974, 1975 and 1985 under Barry Switzer; and 2000 under Bob Stoops.
posts.summary: Oklahoma claims seven football national titles: 1950, 1955, 1956, 1974, 1975, 1985 and 2000. Here's each one, its coach, and the other years OU doesn't claim.

posts.title: Jason White's 2003 Heisman: OU's Comeback Quarterback
posts.question: How did Jason White win the Heisman after two knee injuries?
posts.answer: Jason White, from Tuttle, Oklahoma, tore the ACL in each knee in 2001 and 2002, then threw for 3,744 yards and 40 touchdowns in 2003 to win the Heisman Trophy as Oklahoma's fourth winner.
posts.summary: Tuttle native Jason White came back from two torn ACLs to win the 2003 Heisman with 40 TD passes, then won the Davey O'Brien Award again in 2004.

posts.title: Billy Sims BBQ: How OU's Heisman Winner Built a Restaurant Chain
posts.question: When did Billy Sims open his first Billy Sims BBQ restaurant?
posts.answer: Billy Sims, OU's 1978 Heisman winner, co-founded Billy Sims BBQ with partner Jeff Jackson; the first restaurant opened in Tulsa in 2004.
posts.summary: Heisman winner Billy Sims (OU 1975-79) co-founded Billy Sims BBQ with Jeff Jackson, opening the first one in Tulsa in 2004 before growing to 50-plus units.

posts.title: Oklahoma's 1985 National Title: 25-10 Orange Bowl Win Over Penn State
posts.question: How did Oklahoma win the 1985 national championship?
posts.answer: Oklahoma beat No. 1 Penn State 25-10 in the Orange Bowl on Jan. 1, 1986. With Miami losing to Tennessee in the Sugar Bowl the same day, the Sooners finished No. 1 for Barry Switzer's third national title.
posts.summary: Oklahoma beat No. 1 Penn State 25-10 in the Jan. 1, 1986 Orange Bowl to claim the 1985 national title behind freshman QB Jamelle Holieway and Keith Jackson.

posts.title: Bud Wilkinson's Three National Titles at Oklahoma: 1950, 1955, 1956
posts.question: How many national championships did Bud Wilkinson win at Oklahoma?
posts.answer: Three: 1950, 1955 and 1956. Wilkinson went 145-29-4 at Oklahoma from 1947 through 1963 and won 14 conference championships in 17 seasons.
posts.summary: Bud Wilkinson led Oklahoma to national titles in 1950, 1955 and 1956 and went 145-29-4. A look at each championship team and the coach who built the dynasty.

posts.title: Billy Sims: 1978 Heisman Winner Who Built a BBQ Brand
posts.question: What year did Billy Sims win the Heisman and what did he do after football?
posts.answer: Billy Sims won the 1978 Heisman Trophy as a junior after leading the nation with 1,762 rushing yards. After his NFL career he co-founded Billy Sims Barbecue, which opened its first restaurant in Tulsa in 2004.
posts.summary: Billy Sims won the 1978 Heisman with a nation-best 1,762 rushing yards, went No. 1 in the NFL draft and later co-founded the Billy Sims Barbecue chain.

posts.title: Jack Mildren: Wishbone QB Turned Oklahoma Lieutenant Governor
posts.question: Which OU quarterback became lieutenant governor of Oklahoma?
posts.answer: Jack Mildren, OU's quarterback from 1969 to 1971, was elected Oklahoma lieutenant governor in 1990 and served from 1991 to 1995.
posts.summary: Jack Mildren quarterbacked OU from 1969 to 1971, ran its record-setting wishbone, then became lieutenant governor, a banker and a sports radio host.

posts.title: Barry Switzer's Back-to-Back National Titles: Oklahoma 1974 and 1975
posts.question: Did Oklahoma win back-to-back national championships under Barry Switzer?
posts.answer: Yes. Switzer's 1974 Sooners went 11-0 and won the AP national title despite a bowl ban, and the 1975 team repeated at 11-1 after beating Michigan 14-6 in the Orange Bowl.
posts.summary: Barry Switzer's Sooners won national titles in 1974 and 1975, one under a bowl ban and one capped by a 14-6 Orange Bowl win over Michigan. Here's the story.

posts.title: 1971 Oklahoma Wishbone Set NCAA Rushing Record: 472.4 Yards a Game
posts.question: What NCAA rushing record did Oklahoma's 1971 wishbone offense set?
posts.answer: The 1971 Sooners averaged 472.4 rushing yards per game, 5,196 yards in 11 regular-season games, an NCAA record. Barry Switzer ran the wishbone as offensive coordinator for head coach Chuck Fairbanks.
posts.summary: Oklahoma's 1971 wishbone ran for 472.4 yards a game, an NCAA record. Meet the Sooners offense led by Jack Mildren and Greg Pruitt under Fairbanks and Switzer.

posts.title: Steve Owens and the 1969 Heisman: OU's Workhorse Running Back
posts.question: When did Steve Owens win the Heisman Trophy and what were his stats?
posts.answer: Steve Owens won the 1969 Heisman Trophy after leading the nation in rushing with 1,523 yards and in scoring with 138 points. He was Oklahoma's second Heisman winner, after Billy Vessels.
posts.summary: Steve Owens won the 1969 Heisman after leading the nation with 1,523 rushing yards, then became a Lions star, OU athletic director and Norman businessman.

posts.title: J.C. Watts: From Sooners Quarterback to the U.S. Congress
posts.question: Which former OU quarterback became a U.S. Congressman?
posts.answer: J.C. Watts, OU's starting quarterback in 1979 and 1980, later represented Oklahoma in the U.S. House from 1995 to 2003 and chaired the House Republican Conference.
posts.summary: J.C. Watts led OU to back-to-back Orange Bowl wins, played in the CFL, then served Oklahoma in Congress from 1995 to 2003 and chaired the House GOP Conference.

posts.title: 1971 Game of the Century: Nebraska 35, Oklahoma 31 in Norman
posts.question: Who won the 1971 Game of the Century between Oklahoma and Nebraska?
posts.answer: Nebraska won 35-31 on Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 25, 1971, at Owen Field in Norman. Jeff Kinney's 2-yard touchdown run with 1:38 left decided the matchup of No. 1 Nebraska and No. 2 Oklahoma.
posts.summary: No. 1 Nebraska beat No. 2 Oklahoma 35-31 on Thanksgiving Day 1971 in Norman. Here's how the Game of the Century unfolded, from Rodgers' punt return to Kinney.

posts.title: Oklahoma's 47-Game Winning Streak (1953-57): How It Began and Ended
posts.question: What is the longest winning streak in college football history?
posts.answer: Oklahoma won 47 straight games from October 1953 to November 1957 under Bud Wilkinson, the longest winning streak in Division I history. Notre Dame ended it 7-0 in Norman on Nov. 16, 1957.
posts.summary: Oklahoma's record 47-game winning streak ran from 1953 to 1957 under Bud Wilkinson before Notre Dame ended it 7-0 in Norman. Here's how it started and stopped.

posts.title: Billy Vessels: Oklahoma's First Heisman Trophy Winner in 1952
posts.question: Who was the first Oklahoma Sooner to win the Heisman Trophy?
posts.answer: Halfback Billy Vessels of Cleveland, Oklahoma, won the 1952 Heisman Trophy, the first ever for OU. He ran for 1,072 yards and 17 touchdowns that fall under coach Bud Wilkinson.
posts.summary: Billy Vessels won OU's first Heisman in 1952 with 1,072 rushing yards, then built a second career in Florida real estate and horse racing regulation.
